questions.q: Why does Kumalo go to Pimville alone to see the girl?
choices: He feels he can reach his goal more surely without others, whose pace his slow tribal manner irritates
The girl asked to see only him
questions.explain: He chooses a time when Msimangu cannot come.

questions.q: How does Kumalo break the news to the girl?
choices: He tells her Absalom is in prison 'for the most terrible deed that a man can do' — he has killed a white man
He says nothing and lets her guess
He tells her Absalom has run away again
questions.explain: She does not fully understand at first; she is 'surely but a child.'

questions.q: What does Kumalo leave with the girl, warning her not to show it to others?
What is the girl's family history?
choices: Her father left because her mother was so often drunk; she could not understand her 'second father', so she left and lived in Sophiatown
She was raised by the church
She ran away from a farm
questions.explain: She has had three 'husbands' — the first two were 'caught', and now the third is caught, for murder.

questions.q: In his 'wild and cruel mood', what does Kumalo ask the girl?
choices: Whether she would be willing to be with him — 'Not even, he asked, if I desired you?'
questions.explain: She answers 'I could be willing', and he covers his face, ashamed — 'but for his cruelty, not her compliance.'

choices: She does not know at all
questions.explain: 'I do not know, she sobbed, but I think I am sixteen.'

questions.q: What does the girl say she desires, when Kumalo warns her that life at Ndotsheni is very quiet?
choices: Quietness — 'That shall be my desire... the desire that will be upon me'
questions.explain: Her turning the word 'desire' to mean the wish for peace astonishes him.

questions.q: What one promise does Kumalo ask of the girl?
choices: That if she ever repents of the plan, she will tell him and not shut it up inside her or run away as she did from her mother
To go to church every day
questions.explain: She promises, then adds eagerly, 'I shall never repent.'

questions.q: What church does the girl say she belongs to?
questions.explain: She says it 'eagerly', to please him.

questions.q: How does Kumalo feel as he walks away from the girl at the end of the chapter?
choices: 'Like a man from whom a pain has lifted a little, not altogether, but a little'
Certain his son will be freed
questions.explain: He remembers with a shock that Father Vincent had said, 'I shall pray, night and day.'
